title: Quatrefoil Éclat Studs
category: Earrings (four-point star stud, sold as 1 pair, the 2 studs identical and symmetric, worn with one tip pointing down)
metal: 18k gold tone (listing: PVD 18K gold coating), warm yellow, high mirror polish; small satin-finish recessed panels in the 4 corners of the centre plate; all stones clear cubic zirconia
lock: 2 studs, each a 15 mm four-pointed star with concave sides, worn tip-down. 1 row of about 44 tiny round pavé stones traces the outline. Inside, 4 clear pear-cut stones, each in a polished frame with 1 bead prong at its point, aim out at the 4 tips. Centre: 1 round clear stone in a bezel on a 4-pointed plate. 8 slim open gaps flank the pears. Post, butterfly back. 18k gold tone, high polish. Must stay a sharp four-pointed star with an open pavé outline around 4 outward-pointing pears, never a rounded four-leaf clover or a solid pavé face.
morph: The outline and the fill. The product name ('Quatrefoil') and the listing copy ('four-lobed quatrefoil', 'every lobe filled edge to edge with micro pavé', 'sits flat on the lobe') both push an image model toward a rounded four-leaf clover or a solid pavé disc, which is not what the photos show. Next most likely: the 4 pears become marquises or rounds, or multiply to 5, 6 or 8 petals (a snowflake or flower); the 8 open gaps fill in; the centre bezel and its little 4-pointed plate drop out or turn into a pavé cluster; the pavé outline doubles. Scale also drifts: in the ads-500 study, crazy15 (masala dabba) lost the studs in the prop, and models tend to draw a stud the size of a coin. Keep the prompt words 'four-pointed star', 'pear-cut' and 'open pavé outline' and leave out 'quatrefoil' and 'clover' in image prompts.
sizeMm: 15 mm tip to tip, plus or minus 1 mm (size guide photo 05, which has a 15 mm bar and a 10 mm ruler and is also embedded in the description; the description gives 'approximately 15mm'). Estimated from photo 05: each pear is about 4.5 mm long, the round centre stone about 2.5 mm, and each pavé stone well under 1 mm. Worn (photo 02, close to true scale), the stud sits tip-down and covers most of the earlobe without spreading past it. About the size of a standard shirt button (15 mm), or three quarters of a Rs 1 coin (20 mm).

story: A four-pointed star of light: 4 clear teardrops point north, south, east and west from 1 round stone, inside a glittering pavé outline with small windows of skin showing through. It is the little four-point twinkle a cartoonist draws on something to show that it shines, made real and worn on the earlobe. At 15 mm it fills the lobe and stops there. The founder's styling tip is to let them be the only sparkle, with a plain neckline and the hair tucked behind the ear. The worn photo pairs them with a mustard satin cowl-neck slip and bare collarbones. Shape rhymes: the four-point sparkle glyph; the star filter on 90s Indian wedding videos, which turned every light into a 4-point star; a compass rose; a diamond-shaped patang (kite) at Uttarayan; Mughal jaali and star-and-cross tiles; a four-point star bindi; a paper akash kandil; a shuriken (the crazy end). Already used: star anise in a masala dabba (performance C15 / ads-500 crazy15, where the product got lost in the prop), a Diwali akash kandil (C45, 'Your Diwali star.'), fallen parijat flowers (COLOUR50 #25, 'Collected at dawn.'), a jaali heritage shot (finished-ads quatrefoil1, capped at 8.5 for having no jaali in frame and a dark ground), and the 'not kaju katli' star-versus-rhombus pun (which the Ribbon Bead rhyme ad also uses). Fresh angles: the cartoon glint, the wedding-video star filter, the compass rose, the patang, the shuriken.
copyNotes: Use: 18k gold tone, PVD 18K gold coating (as a material fact only), clear cubic zirconia, four-point star, pavé outline or pavé edge, pear-cut stones, round centre stone, 15 mm tip to tip, one pair, stud with butterfly back, Edition One, pre-order, Rs 1,099. Keep 'Quatrefoil Éclat' as the product name only. Earlier ads proved 'pavé and pear-cut stones.' works as the correction line. Avoid: 'gold' without 'tone', solid, real or 18k gold; diamond, precious, gemstone; four-leaf clover, clover, lobes, 'filled edge to edge with micro pavé' or solid pavé (the listing copy and the 03 alt text say this, but the photos contradict it); snowflake, flower with more than 4 petals, five-, six- or eight-point star; designer comparisons or any other brand's clover or monogram; waterproof, tarnish free, anti-tarnish, sweat-proof, hypoallergenic (the listing has none of those tags, and the description's 'anti-tarnish' line is not a claim we can make in ads); huggie, drop, dangle, climber; any size other than 15 mm; the old price 1,299; 'not kaju katli' (already used twice).

photos.shows: Packshot: the pair on a cream plaster block, warm beige backdrop. The left stud is straight on and the right is angled to show the post and a gold butterfly back with a scalloped edge. 18k gold tone. Shows the whole construction: concave four-point star, single pavé outline, 4 pear stones pointing out, round bezel centre on a 4-pointed plate, open gaps. Reference 1.

Worn, front: lips to collarbone, both ears, studs tip-down on the lobes, mustard satin cowl-neck slip, dark wavy hair, cream backdrop. Close to true 15 mm scale: each stud is about a quarter of the mouth's width. Reference 2 (scale).

Macro of one stud at 3/4 on cream plaster. Clearest detail of the pear frames, bead prongs at the pear points, the raised round bezel, the 4-pointed centre plate with satin corners, and about 11 pavé stones per side. Best construction backup; it has no scale referent. Its alt text repeats the listing's inaccurate 'filled edge to edge' wording.
Packaging: blush Naira gift box on travertine in hard sun. No product.
Size guide: the 01 packshot with a 15 mm bar and a 10 mm ruler; text 'Stud 15 mm, tip to tip', give or take 1 mm. Scale evidence. It has a text overlay, so do not use it as a generation reference.
